title: Passive Voice: Giving Prominence — Quiz 118
content:
## Passive Voice: Giving Prominence

See how the passive changes the focus of a sentence.

### Lesson focus

1. The storm uprooted the old tree last night.
2. The old tree was uprooted by the storm last night.

### Understand the pattern

Word order influences what the reader treats as the topic. Starting with the old tree makes that tree prominent; starting with the storm makes the storm prominent. Both sentences can describe the same event without changing its tense.

### Worked answers and explanation

The storm uprooted the old tree last night → The old tree was uprooted by the storm last night. Keep last night in both versions. The passive is useful in a paragraph already discussing damage to the tree; the active is useful in a paragraph discussing what the storm did.

### Try another

Rewrite with the trophy as the topic: Our team won the trophy.

### Suggested answer

The trophy was won by our team. Won is both the past-simple and past-participle form of win; was marks the passive past tense.
